title: Fragile latency window - all-hands draft & Q&A
body:
Purpose: quick personal scratch for the all-hands segment on the recent fragile latency window (Mar 9-10). Not polished — keep short live script + Q&A crib.

TL;DR (one-liner to read on stage):
- We saw a transient latency window last week affecting ~3% of requests for ~90 minutes; root cause tied to a batching regression in the runtime after a rollout. We reverted the change, capacity autoscaled, and customer impact was limited; engineers are on a 72-hour deep-dive and we'll share follow-ups.

Key points I want to cover (order for 5min segment):
1) What happened (plain English) — high level, no tech jargon for business folks
   - March 9 ~10:15 PST we began seeing P50 stable but P95/P99 spikes at specific routes (chat/generate).
   - Automatic batching heuristics shifted traffic into larger batches; some GPU kernels had longer tail latency for mid-length sequences.
   - Result: request queues grew, some client requests timed out (retries increased) -> visible error rate bump.
2) Immediate response + mitigation we did 
   - Canary rollback of batching heuristic at ~10:45 (route-level fallback).
   - Emergency capacity burst to dedicated pools, traffic reroute to healthy variants.
   - Customer care: proactive emails to ~12 enterprise customers; CS handled 4 escalations.
3) Current status (what we know now)
   - Service fully recovered by 12:00; post-revert metrics show stable P99 back to baseline.
   - No data loss, no security incident.
4) What we are doing next (concrete follow-ups)
   - 72-hour postmortem assigned (owner: Ravi). Live doc: Confluence INF-3421 (link).
   - Hotfix: add deterministic batching tests to CI and synthetic tail-latency suite.
   - Ops: new temporary SLO guard to auto-fallback batching changes if P99 > threshold for >5min.
   - Product: rolling review of rollout guardrails for serving runtime feature flags.

Suggested on-stage script (short):
- "We briefly hit a latency window last Tuesday that affected a small percentage of traffic. Our on-call and infra teams reverted the change and brought services back to normal within about an hour. We reached out to impacted customers and are running a focused investigation to make sure this doesn't recur. More details and next steps will be in the postmortem we’ll publish this week."

Anticipated questions + short answers (crib):
- Q: How many customers were impacted?
  A: ~12 customers saw increased retries; 4 filed support tickets. No widespread behavioral impact for end-users. (Numbers from CS at 11:30).
- Q: Was customer data exposed?
  A: No. No data plane or auth changes occurred.
- Q: Will this affect pricing / credits?
  A: Not expected. If a customer experienced errors and asks for credits, CS will triage case-by-case; we offered proactive outreach.
- Q: Are certain models/regions more vulnerable?
  A: The spike concentrated on medium-length chat sequences and certain model kernels; it was observed in us-west-2 primary cluster. We’re adding targeted tests per model-variant.
- Q: Should customers migrate to Dedicated?
  A: Dedicated offers predictable throughput but this was a software rollout issue; migration is not a substitute for runtime safety — but customers needing isolation and predictability should talk to account teams.

Notes to self / things to double-check before all-hands:
- Confirm CS outreach copy (Inez) — get approval.
- Get final impact counts from Support (ticket list + timeline).
- Confirm wording with Legal on "no data exposed" (quick sign-off).
- Request brief from Release Eng on rollout timeline and how the heuristic got through canary.
- Add link to postmortem draft in slides.

Ops escalation plan (internal only, do not read on stage):
- Owner: Ravi Patel (72h PM)
- Secondary: Inez (CS liaison), Jonas (runtime owner)
- Actions: reproduce locally with synthetic load (test vectors added to infra repo), add CI test for batch-size distribution parity, implement temporary metric guard (P99 latency threshold) to auto-fallback batch changes in the next prod rollout window.

Draft internal announcement (short email / slack for #all-hands):
- Subject: Brief update: transient latency window on Mar 9 (recovered)
- Body: We experienced a transient latency window impacting a small percentage of production requests on Mar 9. The change that triggered this was a batching heuristic rollout in the serving runtime. Engineers reverted the change and the service recovered within ~90 minutes. We’ve opened a 72-hour postmortem (INF-3421) and will publish findings and action items by end of week. If you’re in CS/AM and have customer follow-ups, join the sync at 14:00 today.

Tone guidance for on-stage: calm, accountable, actionable. Avoid technical deep dives; point folks to postmortem for details. Emphasize: we detected it, rolled back, worked with customers, we’re fixing the process.

Open questions / uncertainties I want answered pre-show:
- Exact P95/P99 numbers for affected routes across the 10:15-12:00 window (metrics team).
- Which canary gates missed the rollout (release engineering).
- Are any telemetry blindspots preventing earlier detection?

TODO (my checklist):
- [ ] Finalize the two-sentence TL;DR for stage (by 9am 3/12)
- [ ] Lock CS outreach copy (Inez)
- [ ] Confirm legal wording (privacy/data)
- [ ] Add postmortem link to slides
- [ ] Quick sync with Jonas + Ravi at 10:00

Random scratch reminders (short):
- Keep CEO script <40 words.
- Avoid saying "bug" on stage — prefer "regression in an internal heuristic".
- If asked about auto-rollbacks, say: "we have guardrails; we’ll strengthen them".

End of scratchpad.

(If I circle back: convert to short 3-bullet slide + 3 Q&A bullets; copy to shared_drives/company/misc/ops-comm-drafts directory once approved.)
